haiku-low.q1: The scheduler's 02:00 UTC attempt starts it. It extracts replica orders with updated_at later than the watermark minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk imports stay open up to 90 minutes and get updated_at when written, not committed, so rows can appear up to 90 minutes late.
haiku-low.q3: The edit sets a newer updated_at, so the next night's extract (watermark minus 2 hours) reads it and the merge updates the existing row.
haiku-low.q4: The warehouse keeps the order and sets is_deleted to true. The delete is a write with updated_at, so the normal extract picks it up.
haiku-low.q5: Dashboards keep the last committed night and the watermark stays unchanged. Retry in 15 minutes; after the third failure, page on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the last committed night. A staleness alert is posted to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: Sunday reconciliation finds it by comparing count and checksum per order-creation day for 30 days, then reloads the mismatched day through staging and the merge.
haiku-low.q8: The merge updates an existing row only when the staged updated_at is newer, and keeps the newest row per order_id, so older copies never overwrite.
haiku-low.q9: Stored in etl_watermark. It is set to the larger of the old watermark and the largest updated_at in the extract, in the same transaction as the merge.
haiku-low.q10: The merge and watermark update run in one warehouse transaction, and dashboards read only committed data, so a rollback leaves nothing visible.
haiku-low.q11: Staging is emptied at the start of each attempt, so the failed attempt's staged rows are discarded. The retry uses the same watermark, extracting from watermark minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads that whole day's orders from the replica, applies them through staging and the merge, and does not move the watermark.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts the attempt at 02:00 UTC. It extracts replica orders whose updated_at is later than the watermark minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q2: A bulk import is a large app transaction that can stay open up to 90 minutes. Its rows get updated_at when written, not at commit, so they can appear up to 90 minutes late.
sonnet.q3: The edit sets a new updated_at. The next nightly extract picks it up (it is after watermark minus 2h). The merge updates the fact_orders row because the staged updated_at is newer.
sonnet.q4: The app sets deleted_at, which is a write and bumps updated_at, so the normal extract picks it up. The merge sets is_deleted to true. The order stays in fact_orders.
sonnet.q5: The attempt fails, and staging is discarded (extract failure) or the transaction rolls back (merge or commit failure). Nothing becomes visible and the watermark is unchanged. It retries in 15 minutes, with attempts at 02:00, 02:15 and 02:30. If the third attempt fails, on-call is paged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards refresh anyway and show the last committed night. A staleness alert is posted to #data-alerts.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. For each order-creation day in the last 30 days it compares row count and checksum with the replica. On a mismatch it reloads that whole day through staging and the merge.
sonnet.q8: Staging keeps only the newest updated_at row per order_id. The merge updates an existing fact_orders row only when the staged updated_at is newer, and inserts if the order is new. So older or duplicate copies change nothing.
sonnet.q9: It is stored in the etl_watermark table in the warehouse. The value is the larger of the old watermark and the largest updated_at in this extract. It is written inside the merge transaction, so it moves only when the data commits.
sonnet.q10: The merge and watermark update happen in one warehouse transaction. Dashboards read only committed data, and the load becomes visible only at commit, so they see either the old night or the new one.
sonnet.q11: Staging is emptied at the start of each attempt, so the failed attempt's staged data is discarded. The retry repeats the same steps with the same watermark, so it extracts updated_at later than watermark minus 2 hours, the same window.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads that whole order-creation day from the replica. It applies the rows through staging and the normal merge. It never moves the watermark.
